primary_result: On the isolated 100-canonical-scene, 400-variant Haze4K official-test development partition, the GT-selected 32-by-32 spatial oracle exceeded the GT-selected per-image best uniform oracle from the identical keep/weaken/strengthen action set by a scene-mean 1.9347 dB PSNR (20,000-resample scene bootstrap 95% CI 1.7319 to 2.1418 dB). The lower confidence bound exceeded the frozen +0.10 dB utility threshold. Ninety-eight of 100 scenes achieved at least +0.10 dB spatial-over-uniform gain (Wilson 95% CI 0.9300 to 0.9945), whose lower bound exceeded the frozen 0.20 breadth threshold. Both frozen harm gates passed: SSIM harm occurred in 4/100 scenes (Wilson upper bound 0.0984) and color-bias harm in 3/100 scenes (Wilson upper bound 0.0845), each below the 0.10 maximum upper-bound threshold.
gate_reasons: all 100 canonical clear scenes and 400 nested haze variants completed fixed-checkpoint inference and bounded-oracle evaluation with no failures and no training
the scene-bootstrap lower bound for spatial-minus-best-uniform PSNR was +1.7319 dB, exceeding the frozen +0.10 dB threshold
the Wilson lower bound for scenes gaining at least +0.10 dB was 0.9300, exceeding the frozen 0.20 prevalence threshold
the Wilson upper bound for scene-level SSIM harm was 0.0984, below the frozen 0.10 safety threshold
the Wilson upper bound for scene-level color-bias harm was 0.0845, below the frozen 0.10 safety threshold
the 150-scene candidate-confirmation asset was not delivered or accessed
scientific_interpretation: Within the frozen output-residual action family, spatially varying selection has large and widespread counterfactual headroom beyond an already GT-privileged per-image uniform choice. The coexistence of keep, weaken, and strengthen selections supports a state-dependent action problem rather than a fixed stronger-is-better or weaker-is-safer rule. This result qualifies only the next proxy-predictability experiment: whether hazy input or frozen intermediate features can predict useful local actions or harm risk under scene-level cross-validation. It does not yet establish deployability, justify a specific module, or authorize candidate-confirmation or NH-HAZE access.
competing_explanation: The measured gain may reflect GT optimization of local RGB-MSE over many tiles, content- or regression-error correction, synthetic Haze4K characteristics, the chosen 32-pixel grid, or the official checkpoint's output residual geometry rather than a haze-specific causal mechanism. Tilewise oracle choices are unavailable at deployment and may overstate realizable benefit when action prediction errors, spatial smoothing, perceptual objectives, or network-internal insertion constraints are introduced.
limitations: This is development-screening evidence from 100 isolated Haze4K official-test scenes; it is not the protected 150-scene candidate confirmation or NH-HAZE external validation.
The 400 haze variants are nested within 100 canonical clear scenes; their results were averaged within scene before statistical inference and they are not 400 independent statistical units.
The oracle uses GT to choose both the per-image uniform reference and each local action and is therefore non-deployable.

The tested action family contains only output-residual scales 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 on an origin-aligned 32-by-32 grid; it does not identify an optimal action space, tile scale, smoothing rule, insertion site, loss, or architecture.
PSNR is the primary oracle objective and the frozen SSIM and color gates provide limited safety evidence; perceptual quality and real-haze validity remain unconfirmed.
A headroom PASS authorizes only a separately contracted proxy-predictability test and does not authorize module training, structural selection, confirmation access, or causal mechanism claims.
